newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-homeless devise poor man's Monopoly.
newsitem.headline: French ex-homeless devise poor man's Monopoly.

text.p: Four former homeless men have devised a Monopoly-like game in which players compete to dodge police identity checks, dole queues, debts and the bottle to reach the ultimate goal: a job.
Named SDF -- the French initials for Sans Domicile Fixe or No Fixed Abode -- and packaged in brown cardboard recalling the street shelters of the homeless, the game goes on sale next month.
Homeless-turned-businessman Francis Mariette told France-2 television on Thursday he and his partners hoped to sell 100,000 games by the end of this year and hire 20 homeless people.
"People may think a game about poverty is immoral, but it is not any more shocking than games about finances or real estate," he said.
